summary: Makes API, event processing, sync, webhook and reporting SLOs executable with deterministic load/failure profiles and fail-closed percentile, throughput, lag, saturation and error-budget evaluation.

impacts.evidence: Task 066 evaluates aggregate operational observations and introduces no tenant data store or authorization path.
SLO observations contain only numeric timing/count/capacity signals; payloads, identifiers, headers and credentials are outside the contract.
No public HTTP/OpenAPI operation changes; API objectives are host-side operational contracts.
No event schema changes; Kafka/event-processing lag and throughput are measured around existing envelopes.
Connector SDK/provider contracts remain unchanged and external provider availability is explicitly excluded from host availability SLOs.
No PostgreSQL or ClickHouse schema change is required by the evaluator/baseline harness.
Metric observations are bounded numeric structures; deterministic CI qualification avoids arbitrary payload capture or remote endpoints.
Threshold changes become reviewed repository changes and performance release gates fail closed on a breach rather than silently widening budgets.
Committed baseline and deployment evidence requirements bind measurements to commit/image, topology, dataset and duration.
Sync/reconciliation lag is a first-class objective; deterministic profiles include partial-outage recovery without changing domain idempotency contracts.
Durable webhook delivery receives explicit latency, throughput, lag and availability objectives while external endpoint downtime remains dependency state.
Task 066 defines executable objectives, p50/p95/p99 summarization, throughput, lag, saturation, 30-day error budgets and six deterministic load/failure profiles.
A release is blocked by objective breach; Task 077 owns paging/runbooks and recovery actions while Task 066 supplies the measurable trigger.
make performance regenerates a deterministic baseline and diffs it; tests prove every threshold fails closed and default failure profiles remain inside declared budgets.
